_what: PRE-REGISTERED FAULT SETS. Every rung above `designed` in the delivery machine is earned by one of these, and what makes it evidence is that the faults were named BEFORE the code. checks/stage.mjs reads this file; architecture/theme.json declares the machine it feeds.
_why_here_and_not_in_the_test: A fault list living inside the test file it describes is written by the author of the code, after the code, until it passes — which certifies only that the code does what it does. Kept in a tracked file of its own, a fault added later to turn a rung green is a DIFF a reviewer sees. That is the whole mechanism, and it is adapted from mutation testing's premise that the planted fault is the measurement — with the faults named by hand and in advance, because a mutant generated from the code cannot exist before the code.
_what_it_cannot_do: Nothing observes the ORDER two files were written in. This registry and an implementation can land in one commit and no check here can tell. The rung above is git — the commit that first adds a fault must not be later than the one that first adds the implementation — and it is buildable, not built.
_state_today: 2026-09-07. Every set below carries faults and NO `file`, which is the honest first state: the criteria are written, the defence code is not. checks/stage.mjs reads that as `preregistered, unwritten` and leaves the box at `designed` — it is not a failure, it is the correct order. Fill in `file` when the set is written; the rung moves when git tracks it and it names its subject.
